A method is provided for interacting with content items displayed on a computing device. The method includes displaying a plurality of content items in a list on a display of the computing device, with the list extending along a first direction, such as vertically or horizontally across the display.

The method further includes detecting a first portion of a user gesture. The first gesture portion selects one of the displayed content items by moving, dragging, or swiping the selected content item in a direction that is substantially orthogonal to the first direction of the list. For example, where the list extends vertically, the first gesture portion may include a horizontal drag across the display.

While the content item remains selected, the method detects a second portion of the gesture. The second gesture portion is performed in a direction opposite to the direction of the first gesture portion. In response to detecting this second gesture portion, the method marks at least one content item for deletion. The marked item may include the selected content item and, in some implementations, may include one or more additional content items associated with the gesture.

After the gesture is completed, the method deletes the marked content item or content items. Completion of the gesture may be determined, for example, when the user lifts a finger or stylus from the touch-sensitive display, or otherwise ends the input action.

A related method is also disclosed for simultaneously editing a parameter of at least one content item in a list. In this related method, a user gesture may be used to select one or more content items and modify a parameter associated with the selected item or items, thereby enabling efficient batch editing or simultaneous adjustment of content within the displayed list.
outputs.L4:
The described technology relates to gesture-based techniques for managing items displayed in a list on a computing device, such as a smartphone, tablet, laptop, or other touch-sensitive or pointer-based user interface. In many list-based interfaces, users frequently need to perform actions on individual items or groups of items, such as deleting messages, changing settings, marking entries, adjusting values, or applying edits. Traditional interfaces often require multiple steps, such as selecting an item, opening a menu, choosing an action, and confirming the operation. The methods described here reduce that complexity by allowing the user to perform selection and action in a single continuous gesture.

In one implementation, a list of content items is displayed on the screen. Each content item may represent, for example, an email message, text message, file, contact, task, notification, media item, or other data object. A user begins by dragging a displayed item in a first direction that is generally orthogonal to the direction in which the list scrolls. For example, if the list scrolls vertically, the user may drag an item horizontally. This orthogonal drag causes the corresponding content item to become selected. The selection may be shown visually, such as by highlighting the item, shifting it from its original position, displaying a checkmark, revealing an action area, or otherwise indicating that the item is now active for a further operation.

After selecting the item through the first drag, the user continues the gesture by dragging in an opposite direction. This second drag, performed without requiring the user to lift a finger or otherwise end the interaction, triggers an action associated with the selected item. For instance, dragging an email message to one side may select it, and dragging back in the opposite direction may delete it, archive it, flag it, or apply another predefined command. Because the gesture is continuous, the user can both select and act on the item with a single fluid motion.

The technique may also be extended to multiple list items. A user may drag across or near several items to select them, or may perform a gesture that causes multiple adjacent or related items to be selected. Once one or more items are selected, the opposite-direction portion of the gesture may apply a shared operation to all selected items. This allows batch actions to be performed quickly without requiring separate taps or menu selections for each item.

In addition to deletion, the gesture may be used to edit one or more parameters associated with list items. For example, the gesture may adjust a priority level, change a status, modify a numerical value, alter a category, set a completion state, or update another attribute. In some implementations, the amount, speed, or direction of the drag may correspond to the parameter being modified. Thus, the user may not only select an item but also control the degree or nature of the edit through the same continuous movement.

The system may provide visual feedback during the gesture to help the user understand what action will be performed. As the item is dragged, the interface may display icons, colors, labels, animations, or other indicators showing whether the item is selected, which action is available, and when the action will be executed. Threshold distances may be used so that accidental movements do not immediately trigger actions. For example, the item may become selected only after being dragged a minimum distance in the first direction, and the action may be invoked only after the user drags back past a second threshold in the opposite direction.

The key advantage of this approach is improved efficiency in list-based user interfaces. By combining selection and command execution into a single gesture, the user can manage list items more quickly and with fewer interactions. This is especially useful on touch-based devices, where screen space is limited and repeated menu navigation can be slow or cumbersome. The method enables fast deletion, editing, and batch modification of list items while maintaining an intuitive gesture pattern that can be learned and repeated easily.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a mobile UI gesture that lets users delete list items by dragging an item sideways and then back in the opposite direction, and also mention simultaneous parameter editing for list items.
counterfactuals.output: A mobile user interface method and system are disclosed for managing items in a displayed list. A touch-sensitive display presents a plurality of list items, each associated with one or more editable parameters. In response to detecting a user contact on a selected list item, the selected list item is translated laterally in a first direction relative to the list. When the user subsequently drags the selected list item in a second, opposite direction, the system determines whether the motion satisfies a deletion gesture criterion, such as a displacement threshold, reversal threshold, velocity condition, or combined gesture path. Upon satisfaction of the criterion, the selected list item is removed from the list, optionally with a visual confirmation animation. The interface may further provide, during or in association with the list interaction, simultaneous editing of parameters for one or more list items, including adjustment of values through touch controls, sliders, inline fields, or multi-item parameter controls, thereby enabling deletion and parameter modification within a common list-management interface.

counterfactuals.output:
### Patent-Style Summary

A computer-implemented method is provided for managing selectable content items in a graphical user interface using directional swipe gestures. The method includes displaying, on a touch-sensitive display, a list comprising a plurality of content items. The system detects a lateral swipe gesture applied to a first content item in the list and, in response to determining that the gesture is in a first direction, visually indicates selection of the first content item. The visual indication may include shifting the content item, highlighting the content item, displaying a selection marker, or otherwise distinguishing the item from non-selected items.

The method further includes detecting a subsequent lateral swipe gesture applied to the selected content item in a second direction different from the first direction. In response to the subsequent gesture, the system marks the selected content item for deletion. The marking may include displaying a deletion indicator, changing an appearance of the content item, moving the content item to a deletion state, or presenting a visual confirmation that the item is pending removal.

Upon completion of the deletion gesture, the system deletes the marked content item from an associated data set or content collection. The deletion may be performed automatically when the gesture satisfies one or more completion criteria, such as exceeding a threshold distance, reaching a terminal gesture position, detecting release of touch input, or confirming that the item remains in the deletion state upon gesture completion. Following deletion, the system updates the displayed list to remove the deleted content item and may adjust the positions of remaining list items.

In some implementations, the method distinguishes between selection and deletion operations based on swipe direction, gesture distance, gesture velocity, item state, or a combination thereof. The system may require that an item first be placed in a selected state before a reverse-direction swipe causes the item to be marked for deletion, thereby reducing unintended deletion of content. The method may be implemented by a mobile device, tablet computer, wearable device, or other computing system having a touch-sensitive display and one or more processors configured to execute instructions for detecting gestures, updating item states, and deleting selected content items.
